_comment: Questions a person at a kitchen table would actually type, and the rules
that answer them. Read by tools/check_retrieval.py.
`any` lists acceptable references: retrieval is approximate, several rules
often answer one question, and the question counts as found when any of
them is in the top eight. Every reference here was read in the real
`gap` marks a question retrieval does not answer yet. Those do not fail
the check -- they are written down so the list stays honest about what is
still broken, and the check says so when one starts passing.

questions.ask: what happens when my hit points reach zero?
questions.why: the keyword collision: reach is an ability and a verb

questions.ask: what happens when my life total reaches zero?
questions.why: the rules write 0, a person writes zero

questions.ask: what happens if I reach zero life?
how many creatures can the defender block with?
questions.why: defender is a keyword and also the person blocking

questions.ask: does the attacker or the defender choose blockers?
what does reach do?
questions.why: the keyword sense must survive the fix above

questions.ask: can a creature with reach block a flyer?
what does deathtouch do?
how does trample work when blocked?
what does flying do?
what is first strike?
does defender mean it cannot attack?
what does haste do?
what does vigilance do?
what does menace do?
can a creature that came into play this turn block?
questions.why: the paraphrase map: 302.6 shares no words with the question

questions.ask: can I attack with a creature I just played?
how many hit points do we start with?
when do I untap my creatures?
can two creatures block the same attacker?
what happens to damage at the end of the turn?
can a tapped creature block?
questions.gap: 509.1a says blockers must be *untapped*, which stems to `untap` and not to `tapped`. The question and the rule state the same fact in opposite polarity, and no bag of words bridges that.
